title: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design
supports: Opened with WebFetch (long page read in chunks). 403.5.1 accessible route clear width 36 in (915 mm), 32 in (815 mm) for up to 24 in (610 mm); 304.3 turning space 60 in (1525 mm) circle or T-shape; 305.3 clear floor space 30 x 48 in (760 x 1220 mm); 306.3 knee clearance; 307.2 protruding objects 4 in (100 mm) max between 27 and 80 in (685 and 2030 mm); 308.2.1 and 308.3.1 reach 48 in (1220 mm) high, 15 in (380 mm) low; 404.2.3 door clear width 32 in (815 mm); 225.2.2 self-service shelves on an accessible route, reach ranges not required; 226.1 at least 5% of dining and work surfaces comply; 902.3 dining and work surface tops 28 to 34 in (710 to 865 mm); 904.3 check-out counter 38 in (965 mm) max; 904.4 sales and service counters: a portion at least 36 in (915 mm) long and 36 in (915 mm) max high for a parallel approach, or 30 in (760 mm) long with knee space for a forward approach

title: ADA Update: A Primer for Small Business
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 28 February 2020). Existing businesses open to the public must remove barriers where readily achievable, judged by size and resources, as a continuing duty; alterations must be accessible to the maximum extent feasible, and work starting on or after 15 March 2012 uses the 2010 Standards; Disabled Access Credit for businesses with 30 or fewer full-time employees or $1 million or less revenue; deduction up to $15,000 a year for barrier removal

title: Access to and use of buildings: Approved Document M
publisher: GOV.UK (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 1 October 2024). Statutory guidance for England; Volume 1 dwellings, Volume 2 buildings other than dwellings (2015 edition, 2020 amendment on Changing Places toilets, 2024 amendments incorporated 1 October 2024); Building Safety Regulator has kept it under review since April 2023

title: Approved Document M, Volume 2: Buildings other than dwellings (2015 edition incorporating 2020 and 2024 amendments)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF saved and read with pdftotext). For use in England. Table 2 minimum effective clear door widths (new / existing): straight-on 800 / 750 mm; at right angles from a route at least 1500 mm wide 800 / 750 mm; from a route at least 1200 mm wide 825 / 775 mm; external doors used by the public 1000 / 775 mm. 3.6 reception counters: a section at least 1500 mm wide, surface no higher than 760 mm, knee recess at least 700 mm; manoeuvring space 1200 x 1800 mm with knee recess or 1400 x 2200 mm without. 3.14 corridors at least 1200 mm unobstructed, passing places 1800 mm. 4.16 refreshment facilities: part of a bar or serving counter no higher than 850 mm; all users reach all parts. 4.30 sockets 400 to 1000 mm, switches 400 to 1200 mm. 4.32 avoid glare and large repeating patterns. Visual contrast: light reflectance value difference over 30 points (20 where illuminance exceeds 200 lux). Meeting Part M does not by itself meet Equality Act 2010 duties; material alterations must not make a building less compliant

title: Fire safety: Approved Document B
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 16 September 2026). Statutory fire safety guidance for buildings in England; Volume 1 dwellings, Volume 2 buildings other than dwellings; 2019 edition with later amendments, including amendments that withdraw the BS 476 national classes with a transition period (dates on the page were not clear to me)

title: Building regulations approval
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no date shown). Approval may be needed for many alterations, including replacing fuse boxes and connected electrics, installing plumbed bathrooms, changing electrics near a bath or shower, fixed air-conditioning and replacing windows and doors; check before you change a building; a competent person scheme installer removes the need to apply yourself; apply to the local authority building control or a registered building control approver; penalties for non-compliance

title: Fire safety in the workplace: who's responsible
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no date shown). Anyone with control of non-domestic premises (employer, owner, landlord, occupier) is the 'responsible person'; duties include a fire risk assessment reviewed regularly, fire safety measures, emergency plans and staff training; covers paying guest accommodation such as B&Bs and self-catering lets; new buildings and alterations must meet building regulations; fire and rescue authorities enforce; Scotland and Northern Ireland have different rules

title: Fire safety law and guidance documents for business
supports: Opened with WebFetch (collection updated 4 October 2023). Fire safety risk assessment guides by premises type: offices and shops (12 September 2023), small and medium places of assembly (28 August 2024), sleeping accommodation (12 September 2023); small paying guest accommodation guide listed under small premises

title: Making your small paying guest accommodation safe from fire (accessible version)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 20 January 2025). For small B&Bs, guest houses and self-catering lets under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005: the responsible person must carry out and record a fire risk assessment, reviewed regularly; interlinked smoke alarms in circulation areas, living rooms and bedrooms and heat alarms in kitchens; escape routes kept clear and not used for storage; furniture and furnishings should meet the Furniture and Furnishings (Fire) (Safety) Regulations 1988, usually shown by a label; do not provide candles, tea lights or ethanol burners

title: 29 CFR 1910.36: Design and construction requirements for exit routes
publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Exit access at least 28 in (71.1 cm) wide at all points; exit route ceiling at least 7 ft 6 in; objects must not reduce the route below minimum width; exit doors open from inside without keys, tools or special knowledge; at least two exit routes unless one allows safe evacuation

title: 29 CFR 1910.37: Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes
publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Exit routes free and unobstructed, with no materials or equipment placed in them; no highly flammable furnishings or decorations in routes; exit doors free of decorations or signs that obscure them; exits marked 'Exit' in letters at least 6 in high; doors that could be mistaken for exits marked 'Not an Exit' or by their use; routes adequately lit; routes kept available during repairs

title: Directive 89/654/EEC: workplace requirements
publisher: European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 19 March 2021). Directive of 30 November 1989 on minimum safety and health requirements for workplaces, the first individual directive under Framework Directive 89/391/EEC; annexes cover emergency routes and exits, traffic routes, and natural and artificial lighting; national laws give detail

title: Lighting at work (HSG38), second edition
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF saved and read with pdftotext; published 1997, free download). Table of recommended average and minimum illuminance for health and safety: movement of people in corridors and circulation routes 20 / 5 lux; work needing limited perception of detail, such as kitchens, 100 / 50 lux; work needing perception of detail, such as offices, 200 / 100 lux; fine detail 500 / 200 lux; avoid large jumps between adjacent areas; glare guidance; points to the CIBSE Code for lighting for design detail

title: Duty to manage asbestos in buildings
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 1 March 2021). The dutyholder (owner, landlord or whoever is responsible for maintenance) must manage asbestos in all non-domestic premises, such as factories or shops, and the common parts of multi-occupancy domestic buildings, including arranging a survey and making a plan

title: Lead Renovation, Repair and Painting Program
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 17 June 2026). Anyone paid to do work that disturbs paint in housing or child-occupied facilities (such as child care and preschools) built before 1978 must be EPA lead-safe certified, including sole traders, and follow lead-safe work practices; homeowners working on their own homes are generally not covered unless they rent out the home

title: Volatile Organic Compounds' Impact on Indoor Air Quality
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 23 June 2026). Paints, varnishes, strippers, building materials and furnishings release VOCs; increase ventilation when using such products, follow label precautions, buy only what you will use soon and dispose of leftovers safely

title: Product Safety Alerts, Reports and Recalls
publisher: Office for Product Safety and Standards, GOV.UK
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Searchable database of UK product safety alerts, reports and recalls (3,822 reports at the time), filterable by risk level, product category, measure and date, with email alerts; most recent entries dated 6 November 2026

title: Product Recall: Argos Habitat Eton Fabric Sofas and Footstools in Grey and Charcoal (2303-0003)
publisher: Office for Product Safety and Standards, GOV.UK
supports: Opened with WebFetch (8 March 2023). Habitat Eton sofas and footstools sold by Argos from 1 February 2022 to 28 February 2023 recalled from end users; the fabric could catch fire and keep burning, failed BS 5852 and did not meet the Furniture and Furnishings (Fire) (Safety) Regulations 1988; risk level serious; notified by local authority Trading Standards

title: Clothing Storage Units
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no date shown). STURDY Act rule (16 CFR part 1261) for free-standing clothing storage units at least 27 in tall, at least 30 lb and with at least 3.2 cubic feet of enclosed storage, made after 1 September 2023: stability tests, an anti-tip device in the box and warning labels; covers chests, dressers and armoires; excludes bookcases, office and dining furniture and built-in units

title: Recalls and Product Safety Warnings
supports: Opened with WebFetch. US recall list with hazard, remedy and units; search filters include Furniture and 'Dressers, Desks, Chests and Buffets'; updated weekly, latest entries 5 November 2026

title: Product safety
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The General Product Safety Regulation aims to keep only safe products on the EU market; Safety Gate is the EU rapid alert system for dangerous non-food products, shared between the Commission and national authorities

title: Measuring Distance

title: Importing and Using 2D Images
